# A real model, release and assay

DepMap provides evidence of genes required for cell growth. Here we match
ScreenR's bundled K562 screen to **K-562, ACH-000551**, in **DepMap 24Q2
Public**, Figshare dataset **25880521**. This is an explicitly pinned archived
release, not a claim to have verified the current release.

The ScreenR data are an **shRNA** dropout screen (Morgens et al., 2016),
comparing the plasmid library with two replicates after 14 days. The DepMap
reference is **CRISPR knockout** data. This is a cross-assay consistency check,
not same-assay validation. Knockdown and knockout differ, and cell culture,
libraries and release processing can also change the comparison. The bundled
screen is a selected subset enriched for previously defined reference genes;
its quality metrics do not estimate performance over an unselected genome.

Dependencies are **positive references for dropout**: disrupting a gene
needed for growth should deplete its barcodes. Genes with low dependency
probability are **candidate non-dependent genes**, hence potential neutral
references. They are not proven neutral under a new treatment: a baseline
non-dependency may become a treatment-specific dependency, and baseline
dependencies can change too.

# Read the offline example and inspect provenance

The package includes a small, real single-model subset of the three original
release files. All 18,443 gene columns, including missing measurements, are
retained. Only other models were removed and the files compressed. This lets
all computations below run offline during ordinary package checks, without
requiring the optional `depmap` package. It is not synthetic data.

```{r reference}
example_dir <- system.file("extdata", "depmap-24Q2-K562", package = "ScreenR")
file_names <- c("CRISPRGeneDependency.csv", "CRISPRGeneEffect.csv", "Model.csv")
files <- setNames(file.path(example_dir, paste0(file_names, ".gz")), file_names)
reference <- get_depmap_reference(
    "ACH-000551", files = files, release = "DepMap 24Q2 Public",
    source = paste("Single-model subset of Figshare dataset 25880521;",
        "https://doi.org/10.25452/figshare.plus.25880521")
)
reference$provenance[c("model_id", "cell_line_name", "release", "source")]
```

The helper returns `essential`, `nonessential`, `genes` and `provenance`.
`GeneEffect` is a continuous Chronos score; `DependencyProbability` is a
separate probability, **not a p-value or FDR**. Do not substitute the legacy
`depmap_crispr()` column named `dependency`, which contains gene effects.

With the default thresholds, probability >= 0.5 selects candidate essential
genes and probability <= 0.1 selects candidate non-dependent genes. Values
between the cutoffs, missing measurements, and invalid or ambiguous gene
identifiers stay unclassified. These cutoffs select reference sets; they do
not calibrate ScreenR's statistical tests.

```{r reference-sets}
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(reference$genes$Class)),
    col.names = c("DepMap class", "Genes"))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(c(reference$essential, reference$nonessential)),
    all(reference$genes$Class[is.na(reference$genes$DependencyProbability)] ==
        "unclassified"))
head(reference$genes[reference$genes$Class == "essential", ])
head(reference$genes[reference$genes$Class == "nonessential", ])
```

The original files were retrieved by the implementation's package-managed
cache and reused here on 2026-11-14. Upstream attribution: **Broad DepMap,
Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT (2024), DepMap 24Q2 Public**, licensed
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/),
[release DOI](https://doi.org/10.25452/figshare.plus.25880521).
The accompanying `README.md` describes the extraction. The original source
file IDs/checksums and derived subset checksums are deliberately separate:

```{r file-provenance}
manifest <- read.delim(file.path(example_dir, "provenance.tsv"),
    colClasses = "character")
stopifnot(identical(unname(tools::md5sum(files)), manifest$derived_md5),
    identical(reference$provenance$files$md5, manifest$derived_md5))
knitr::kable(manifest[c("source_name", "figshare_file_id", "source_md5")])
knitr::kable(manifest[c("derived_file", "derived_md5")])
```

For `files=`, the returned `dataset_id` and file IDs are `NA`: this route
computes checksums for the supplied subset, rather than claiming it read the
original full matrices. The manifest above links those subsets to the source
release. Save the object with `saveRDS(reference, "K562-24Q2-reference.rds")`
and reuse it with `readRDS()` to avoid parsing the same files repeatedly.

# Prepare the bundled shRNA screen

```{r screen}
data(k562_count_table)
data(k562_annotation_table)
samples <- data.frame(
    Sample = c("Plasmid", "T14_A", "T14_B"),
    Day = c("Plasmid", "T14", "T14"), Treatment = "Untreated"
)
k562 <- create_screenr_object(
    table = k562_count_table, annotation = k562_annotation_table,
    groups = factor(c("Plasmid", "T14", "T14")), sample_table = samples
)
k562 <- compute_data_table(normalize_data(k562))
metrics <- compute_metrics(k562, control = "Plasmid", treatment = "T14",
    condition_column = "Day")
```

# Match genes and report unknowns

The helper preserves symbols and Entrez IDs. For a symbol join, remove
**every occurrence** of a duplicated symbol: selecting its first occurrence
would silently choose a biological identity. A hit with an ambiguous or
absent symbol must retain unknown annotations. If the screen has verified
current Entrez IDs, prefer a join on both `Gene` and `EntrezID`; investigate
identifier disagreements rather than guessing aliases.

```{r coverage}
genes <- reference$genes
safe <- genes[!(duplicated(genes$Gene) |
    duplicated(genes$Gene, fromLast = TRUE)), ]
screen_genes <- distinct(metrics, Gene)
matched <- left_join(screen_genes, safe, by = "Gene")
stopifnot(nrow(matched) == nrow(screen_genes))
coverage <- matched %>%
    mutate(Status = case_when(
        is.na(Class) ~ "Absent or ambiguous symbol",
        is.na(DependencyProbability) ~ "Matched; probability missing",
        Class == "unclassified" ~ "Matched; unclassified",
        TRUE ~ Class
    )) %>% count(Status, name = "Screen gene labels")
knitr::kable(coverage)
head(matched %>% filter(is.na(Class) | Class == "unclassified"))
```

There are `r sum(!is.na(matched$Class))` unambiguous symbol matches among
`r nrow(matched)` screen labels; `r sum(is.finite(matched$DependencyProbability))`
have finite dependency probabilities. The screen's `non-targeting` label is
a control, not a biological gene, and correctly has no DepMap annotation.
Missing or unmatched genes never become non-dependent references.

# Check reference separation and scale scores

```{r quality}
quality <- compute_screen_quality(metrics,
    reference$essential, reference$nonessential)
knitr::kable(data.frame(Metric = names(quality),
    Value = unname(unlist(quality))), digits = 3)
```

These metrics use gene means of the barcode log2 fold changes, restricted to
the references actually present in the screen. More negative NNMD and
Cohen's d indicate stronger depletion of dependencies; AUC above 0.5 means
dependencies tend to have lower scores. They describe separation, not a
hypothesis test or proof of treatment neutrality.

```{r separation, fig.alt="K562 shRNA gene score densities: DepMap CRISPR dependency candidates are more depleted than non-dependent candidates."}
plot_reference_separation(metrics, reference$essential, reference$nonessential)
```

The plot's label "Non-essential" means the candidate non-dependent set
selected above. In this example the essential median is below the
non-dependent median, so a reference scale has the intended orientation:

```{r scaling}
gene_means <- metrics %>% group_by(Gene) %>%
    summarise(Log2FC = mean(Log2FC[is.finite(Log2FC)]), .groups = "drop")
anchors <- c(
    essential = median(gene_means$Log2FC[
        gene_means$Gene %in% reference$essential]),
    nondependent = median(gene_means$Log2FC[
        gene_means$Gene %in% reference$nonessential])
)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(anchors)), anchors[[1]] < anchors[[2]])
scaled <- scale_by_reference(metrics, reference$essential, reference$nonessential)
scaled_means <- scaled %>% group_by(Gene) %>%
    summarise(ScaledLog2FC = mean(ScaledLog2FC), .groups = "drop")
scaled_anchors <- c(
    essential = median(scaled_means$ScaledLog2FC[
        scaled_means$Gene %in% reference$essential]),
    nondependent = median(scaled_means$ScaledLog2FC[
        scaled_means$Gene %in% reference$nonessential])
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(Reference = names(anchors),
    OriginalMedian = unname(anchors), ScaledMedian = unname(scaled_anchors)),
    digits = 3)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(scaled_anchors), c(-1, 0), tolerance = 1e-8)))
```

A scaled score of -1 means depletion like the median of this essential set;
0 anchors the median of the candidate non-dependent set. These are rescaled
shRNA scores, not Chronos gene effects or probabilities. Use scaling only
when the sets separate and their biological interpretation fits the contrast.
Do not use a neutral anchor whose genes respond to the treatment.

# Annotate ScreenR hits

Call hits with ScreenR's existing method and defaults, then add DepMap
annotations. Here CAMERA compares T14 with the plasmid library; DepMap does
not change the test, barcode threshold or default FDR cutoff.

```{r annotated-hits}
design <- create_design_matrix(k562)
contrast <- create_contrast(design, treatment = "T14", control = "Plasmid")
hits <- find_camera_hit(k562, design, contrast)
annotated_hits <- left_join(hits, safe, by = "Gene")
stopifnot(nrow(annotated_hits) == nrow(hits))
knitr::kable(head(annotated_hits %>%
    select(Gene, PValue, FDR, DependencyProbability, GeneEffect, Class) %>%
    mutate(across(c(PValue, FDR), ~ format(.x, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3))), 10),
    digits = 4)
knitr::kable(annotated_hits %>%
    count(Class, name = "Hits", .drop = FALSE))
```

CAMERA returns `r nrow(hits)` hits with its defaults here;
`r sum(is.na(annotated_hits$Class))` have unknown symbol annotations. A hit
without a DepMap dependency remains a ScreenR hit. Different assays, release
contexts and identifier changes can explain disagreement.

The dependency set supplies positive references; it is not a null control
set. A candidate non-dependent set may be considered for the existing
`find_gene_zscore_hit(..., reference = "random", control_genes = ...)`
interface only after assessing neutrality for that particular contrast.
This vignette does not substitute it for the empirical null:
`reference = "empirical"` continues to reject `control_genes`, and all
hit-calling defaults remain intact. No dependency probability is interpreted
as a ScreenR p-value.

# Retrieve another release without repeated downloads

The following optional acquisition recipes are **not run during rendering**;
all analysis chunks above execute against real bundled data. An archived
release can be retrieved once through the supported Bioconductor package's
cache (approximately 830 MB for these three full files):

```{r archived-download, eval=FALSE}
# Requires depmap >= 1.19.1 with DepMapFiles() and dmget().
full_reference <- get_depmap_reference("ACH-000551", dataset_id = 25880521)
saveRDS(full_reference, "K562-24Q2-reference.rds")
# In subsequent sessions:
full_reference <- readRDS("K562-24Q2-reference.rds")
full_reference$provenance
```

The package-managed download path records original Figshare file IDs and
checksums. Repeated calls reuse the `depmap` file cache, but still scan the
matrices; reusing the saved reference object avoids those scans too. Do not
download guide-level or raw screens for this workflow.

On R 4.3/Bioconductor 3.18, the standard Bioconductor installation supplies
`depmap` 1.16, which lacks the required APIs. Use a newer compatible
R/Bioconductor, the `files=` route above, or the source revision verified in
this implementation environment:

```{r optional-install, eval=FALSE}
remotes::install_github(
    "UCLouvain-CBIO/depmap@735fa8971fd79ec746a43d354073701b3165e58d"
)
```

For a newer release, obtain its official files from the
[DepMap portal](https://depmap.org/portal/data_page/), keep all three from the
same release, and supply their actual paths, release label and source:

```{r portal-files, eval=FALSE}
# Set these to the files and release you actually downloaded.
portal_files <- setNames(file.path("/path/to/release", file_names), file_names)
portal_reference <- get_depmap_reference("ACH-000551", files = portal_files,
    release = "YOUR VERIFIED RELEASE LABEL", source = "YOUR OFFICIAL SOURCE URL")
portal_reference$provenance
```

**26Q3 file schemas were not verified in this run**: the official metadata
endpoint required human verification. This example verifies the 24Q2 layout
only, with models in rows and `SYMBOL (EntrezID)` gene columns. Inspect newer
headers, model identity, coverage and checksums before using the result;
a changed format requires checking compatibility rather than relabeling
24Q2 as a newer release. No release or assay fallback occurs.

# Sources and session

- Broad DepMap (2024). [DepMap 24Q2 Public](https://doi.org/10.25452/figshare.plus.25880521).
- Morgens DW et al. (2016). [Systematic comparison of CRISPR/Cas9 and RNAi
  screens for essential genes](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3567).
- Tsherniak A et al. (2017). [Defining a cancer dependency map](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.06.010).
- [depmap file retrieval and cache documentation](https://uclouvain-cbio.github.io/depmap/reference/DepMapFiles.html).
